15: /-!
16: # Maximum modulus principle
17: 
18: In this file we prove several versions of the maximum modulus principle. There are several
19: statements that can be called "the maximum modulus principle" for maps between normed complex
20: spaces. They differ by assumptions on the domain (any space, a nontrivial space, a finite
21: dimensional space), assumptions on the codomain (any space, a strictly convex space), and by
22: conclusion (either equality of norms or of the values of the function).
23: 
24: ## Main results
25: 
26: ### Theorems for any codomain
27: 
28: Consider a function `f : E → F` that is complex differentiable on a set `s`, is continuous on its
29: closure, and `‖f x‖` has a maximum on `s` at `c`. We prove the following theorems.
30: 
31: - `Complex.norm_eqOn_closedBall_of_isMaxOn`: if `s = Metric.ball c r`, then `‖f x‖ = ‖f c‖` for
32:   any `x` from the corresponding closed ball;
33: 
34: - `Complex.norm_eq_norm_of_isMaxOn_of_ball_subset`: if `Metric.ball c (dist w c) ⊆ s`, then
35:   `‖f w‖ = ‖f c‖`;
36: 
37: - `Complex.norm_eqOn_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn`: if `U` is an open (pre)connected set, `f` is
38:   complex differentiable on `U`, and `‖f x‖` has a maximum on `U` at `c ∈ U`, then `‖f x‖ = ‖f c‖`
39:   for all `x ∈ U`;
40: 
41: - `Complex.norm_eqOn_closure_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn`: if `s` is open and (pre)connected
42:   and `c ∈ s`, then `‖f x‖ = ‖f c‖` for all `x ∈ closure s`;
43: 
44: - `Complex.norm_eventually_eq_of_isLocalMax`: if `f` is complex differentiable in a neighborhood
45:   of `c` and `‖f x‖` has a local maximum at `c`, then `‖f x‖` is locally a constant in a
46:   neighborhood of `c`.
47: 
48: ### Theorems for a strictly convex codomain
49: 
50: If the codomain `F` is a strictly convex space, then in the lemmas from the previous section we can
51: prove `f w = f c` instead of `‖f w‖ = ‖f c‖`, see
52: `Complex.eqOn_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn_norm`,
53: `Complex.eqOn_closure_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn_norm`,
54: `Complex.eq_of_isMaxOn_of_ball_subset`, `Complex.eqOn_closedBall_of_isMaxOn_norm`, and
55: `Complex.eventually_eq_of_isLocalMax_norm`.
56: 
57: ### Values on the frontier
58: 
59: Finally, we prove some corollaries that relate the (norm of the) values of a function on a set to
60: its values on the frontier of the set. All these lemmas assume that `E` is a nontrivial space.  In
61: this section `f g : E → F` are functions that are complex differentiable on a bounded set `s` and
62: are continuous on its closure. We prove the following theorems.
63: 
64: - `Complex.exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_norm`: If `E` is a finite-dimensional space and `s` is a
65:   nonempty bounded set, then there exists a point `z ∈ frontier s` such that `(‖f ·‖)` takes it
66:   maximum value on `closure s` at `z`.
67: 
68: - `Complex.norm_le_of_forall_mem_frontier_norm_le`: if `‖f z‖ ≤ C` for all `z ∈ frontier s`, then
69:   `‖f z‖ ≤ C` for all `z ∈ s`; note that this theorem does not require `E` to be a
70:   finite-dimensional space.
71: 
72: - `Complex.eqOn_closure_of_eqOn_frontier`: if `f x = g x` on the frontier of `s`, then `f x = g x`
73:   on `closure s`;
74: 
75: - `Complex.eqOn_of_eqOn_frontier`: if `f x = g x` on the frontier of `s`, then `f x = g x`
76:   on `s`.
77: 
78: ## Tags
79: 
80: maximum modulus principle, complex analysis
81: -/

100: ### Auxiliary lemmas
101: 
102: We split the proof into a series of lemmas. First we prove the principle for a function `f : ℂ → F`
103: with an additional assumption that `F` is a complete space, then drop unneeded assumptions one by
104: one.
105: 
106: The lemmas with names `*_auxₙ` are considered to be private and should not be used outside of this
107: file.
108: -/
109: 
110: theorem norm_max_aux₁ [CompleteSpace F] {f : ℂ → F} {z w : ℂ}
111:     (hd : DiffContOnCl ℂ f (ball z (dist w z)))
112:     (hz : IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) (closedBall z (dist w z)) z) : ‖f w‖ = ‖f z‖ := by
113:   -- Consider a circle of radius `r = dist w z`.
114:   set r : ℝ := dist w z
115:   have hw : w ∈ closedBall z r := mem_closedBall.2 le_rfl
116:   -- Assume the converse. Since `‖f w‖ ≤ ‖f z‖`, we have `‖f w‖ < ‖f z‖`.
117:   refine (isMaxOn_iff.1 hz _ hw).antisymm (not_lt.1 ?_)
118:   rintro hw_lt : ‖f w‖ < ‖f z‖
119:   have hr : 0 < r := dist_pos.2 (ne_of_apply_ne (norm ∘ f) hw_lt.ne)
120:   -- Due to Cauchy integral formula, it suffices to prove the following inequality.
121:   suffices ‖∮ ζ in C(z, r), (ζ - z)⁻¹ • f ζ‖ < 2 * π * ‖f z‖ by
122:     refine this.ne ?_
123:     have A : (∮ ζ in C(z, r), (ζ - z)⁻¹ • f ζ) = (2 * π * I : ℂ) • f z :=
124:       hd.circleIntegral_sub_inv_smul (mem_ball_self hr)
125:     simp [A, norm_smul, Real.pi_pos.le]
126:   suffices ‖∮ ζ in C(z, r), (ζ - z)⁻¹ • f ζ‖ < 2 * π * r * (‖f z‖ / r) by
127:     rwa [mul_assoc, mul_div_cancel₀ _ hr.ne'] at this
128:   /- This inequality is true because `‖(ζ - z)⁻¹ • f ζ‖ ≤ ‖f z‖ / r` for all `ζ` on the circle and
129:     this inequality is strict at `ζ = w`. -/
130:   have hsub : sphere z r ⊆ closedBall z r := sphere_subset_closedBall
131:   refine circleIntegral.norm_integral_lt_of_norm_le_const_of_lt hr ?_ ?_ ⟨w, rfl, ?_⟩
132:   · show ContinuousOn (fun ζ : ℂ => (ζ - z)⁻¹ • f ζ) (sphere z r)
133:     refine ((continuousOn_id.sub continuousOn_const).inv₀ ?_).smul (hd.continuousOn_ball.mono hsub)
134:     exact fun ζ hζ => sub_ne_zero.2 (ne_of_mem_sphere hζ hr.ne')
135:   · show ∀ ζ ∈ sphere z r, ‖(ζ - z)⁻¹ • f ζ‖ ≤ ‖f z‖ / r
136:     rintro ζ hζ
137:     rw [le_div_iff₀ hr, norm_smul, norm_inv, mem_sphere_iff_norm.1 hζ, mul_comm,
138:       mul_inv_cancel_left₀ hr.ne']
139:     exact hz (hsub hζ)
140:   show ‖(w - z)⁻¹ • f w‖ < ‖f z‖ / r
141:   rw [norm_smul, norm_inv, ← div_eq_inv_mul, ← dist_eq_norm]
142:   exact (div_lt_div_iff_of_pos_right hr).2 hw_lt
143: 
144: /-!
145: Now we drop the assumption `CompleteSpace F` by embedding `F` into its completion.
146: -/
147: 
148: theorem norm_max_aux₂ {f : ℂ → F} {z w : ℂ} (hd : DiffContOnCl ℂ f (ball z (dist w z)))
149:     (hz : IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) (closedBall z (dist w z)) z) : ‖f w‖ = ‖f z‖ := by
150:   set e : F →L[ℂ] F̂ := UniformSpace.Completion.toComplL
151:   have he : ∀ x, ‖e x‖ = ‖x‖ := UniformSpace.Completion.norm_coe
152:   replace hz : IsMaxOn (norm ∘ e ∘ f) (closedBall z (dist w z)) z := by
153:     simpa only [IsMaxOn, Function.comp_def, he] using hz
154:   simpa only [he, Function.comp_def]
155:     using norm_max_aux₁ (e.differentiable.comp_diffContOnCl hd) hz
156: 
157: /-!
158: Then we replace the assumption `IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) (Metric.closedBall z r) z` with a seemingly
159: weaker assumption `IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) (Metric.ball z r) z`.
160: -/
161: 
162: theorem norm_max_aux₃ {f : ℂ → F} {z w : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : dist w z = r)
163:     (hd : DiffContOnCl ℂ f (ball z r)) (hz : IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) (ball z r) z) : ‖f w‖ = ‖f z‖ := by
164:   subst r
165:   rcases eq_or_ne w z with (rfl | hne); · rfl
166:   rw [← dist_ne_zero] at hne
167:   exact norm_max_aux₂ hd (closure_ball z hne ▸ hz.closure hd.continuousOn.norm)
168: 
169: /-!
170: ### Maximum modulus principle for any codomain
171: 
172: If we do not assume that the codomain is a strictly convex space, then we can only claim that the
173: **norm** `‖f x‖` is locally constant.
174: -/
175: 
176: /-!
177: Finally, we generalize the theorem from a disk in `ℂ` to a closed ball in any normed space.
178: -/
179: 
180: /-- **Maximum modulus principle** on a closed ball: if `f : E → F` is continuous on a closed ball,
181: is complex differentiable on the corresponding open ball, and the norm `‖f w‖` takes its maximum
182: value on the open ball at its center, then the norm `‖f w‖` is constant on the closed ball. -/
183: theorem norm_eqOn_closedBall_of_isMaxOn {f : E → F} {z : E} {r : ℝ}
184:     (hd : DiffContOnCl ℂ f (ball z r)) (hz : IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) (ball z r) z) :
185:     EqOn (norm ∘ f) (const E ‖f z‖) (closedBall z r) := by
186:   intro w hw
187:   rw [mem_closedBall, dist_comm] at hw
188:   rcases eq_or_ne z w with (rfl | hne); · rfl
189:   set e := (lineMap z w : ℂ → E)
190:   have hde : Differentiable ℂ e := (differentiable_id.smul_const (w - z)).add_const z
191:   suffices ‖(f ∘ e) (1 : ℂ)‖ = ‖(f ∘ e) (0 : ℂ)‖ by simpa [e]
192:   have hr : dist (1 : ℂ) 0 = 1 := by simp
193:   have hball : MapsTo e (ball 0 1) (ball z r) := by
194:     refine ((lipschitzWith_lineMap z w).mapsTo_ball (mt nndist_eq_zero.1 hne) 0 1).mono
195:       Subset.rfl ?_
196:     simpa only [lineMap_apply_zero, mul_one, coe_nndist] using ball_subset_ball hw
197:   exact norm_max_aux₃ hr (hd.comp hde.diffContOnCl hball)
198:       (hz.comp_mapsTo hball (lineMap_apply_zero z w))
199: 
200: /-- **Maximum modulus principle**: if `f : E → F` is complex differentiable on a set `s`, the norm
201: of `f` takes it maximum on `s` at `z`, and `w` is a point such that the closed ball with center `z`
202: and radius `dist w z` is included in `s`, then `‖f w‖ = ‖f z‖`. -/
203: theorem norm_eq_norm_of_isMaxOn_of_ball_subset {f : E → F} {s : Set E} {z w : E}
204:     (hd : DiffContOnCl ℂ f s) (hz : IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) s z) (hsub : ball z (dist w z) ⊆ s) :
205:     ‖f w‖ = ‖f z‖ :=
206:   norm_eqOn_closedBall_of_isMaxOn (hd.mono hsub) (hz.on_subset hsub) (mem_closedBall.2 le_rfl)
207: 
208: /-- **Maximum modulus principle**: if `f : E → F` is complex differentiable in a neighborhood of `c`
209: and the norm `‖f z‖` has a local maximum at `c`, then `‖f z‖` is locally constant in a neighborhood
210: of `c`. -/
211: theorem norm_eventually_eq_of_isLocalMax {f : E → F} {c : E}
212:     (hd : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 c, DifferentiableAt ℂ f z) (hc : IsLocalMax (norm ∘ f) c) :
213:     ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝 c, ‖f y‖ = ‖f c‖ := by
214:   rcases nhds_basis_closedBall.eventually_iff.1 (hd.and hc) with ⟨r, hr₀, hr⟩
215:   exact nhds_basis_closedBall.eventually_iff.2
216:     ⟨r, hr₀, norm_eqOn_closedBall_of_isMaxOn (DifferentiableOn.diffContOnCl fun x hx =>
217:         (hr <| closure_ball_subset_closedBall hx).1.differentiableWithinAt) fun x hx =>
218:       (hr <| ball_subset_closedBall hx).2⟩
219: 
220: theorem isOpen_setOf_mem_nhds_and_isMaxOn_norm {f : E → F} {s : Set E}
221:     (hd : DifferentiableOn ℂ f s) : IsOpen {z | s ∈ 𝓝 z ∧ IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) s z} := by
222:   refine isOpen_iff_mem_nhds.2 fun z hz => (eventually_eventually_nhds.2 hz.1).and ?_
223:   replace hd : ∀ᶠ w in 𝓝 z, DifferentiableAt ℂ f w := hd.eventually_differentiableAt hz.1
224:   exact (norm_eventually_eq_of_isLocalMax hd <| hz.2.isLocalMax hz.1).mono fun x hx y hy =>
225:     le_trans (hz.2 hy).out hx.ge
226: 
227: /-- **Maximum modulus principle** on a connected set. Let `U` be a (pre)connected open set in a
228: complex normed space. Let `f : E → F` be a function that is complex differentiable on `U`. Suppose
229: that `‖f x‖` takes its maximum value on `U` at `c ∈ U`. Then `‖f x‖ = ‖f c‖` for all `x ∈ U`. -/
230: theorem norm_eqOn_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn {f : E → F} {U : Set E} {c : E}
231:     (hc : IsPreconnected U) (ho : IsOpen U) (hd : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hcU : c ∈ U)
232:     (hm : IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) U c) : EqOn (norm ∘ f) (const E ‖f c‖) U := by
233:   set V := U ∩ {z | IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) U z}
234:   have hV : ∀ x ∈ V, ‖f x‖ = ‖f c‖ := fun x hx => le_antisymm (hm hx.1) (hx.2 hcU)
235:   suffices U ⊆ V from fun x hx => hV x (this hx)
236:   have hVo : IsOpen V := by
237:     simpa only [ho.mem_nhds_iff, setOf_and, setOf_mem_eq]
238:       using isOpen_setOf_mem_nhds_and_isMaxOn_norm hd
239:   have hVne : (U ∩ V).Nonempty := ⟨c, hcU, hcU, hm⟩
240:   set W := U ∩ {z | ‖f z‖ ≠ ‖f c‖}
241:   have hWo : IsOpen W := hd.continuousOn.norm.isOpen_inter_preimage ho isOpen_ne
242:   have hdVW : Disjoint V W := disjoint_left.mpr fun x hxV hxW => hxW.2 (hV x hxV)
243:   have hUVW : U ⊆ V ∪ W := fun x hx =>
244:     (eq_or_ne ‖f x‖ ‖f c‖).imp (fun h => ⟨hx, fun y hy => (hm hy).out.trans_eq h.symm⟩)
245:       (And.intro hx)
246:   exact hc.subset_left_of_subset_union hVo hWo hdVW hUVW hVne
247: 
248: /-- **Maximum modulus principle** on a connected set. Let `U` be a (pre)connected open set in a
249: complex normed space.  Let `f : E → F` be a function that is complex differentiable on `U` and is
250: continuous on its closure. Suppose that `‖f x‖` takes its maximum value on `U` at `c ∈ U`. Then
251: `‖f x‖ = ‖f c‖` for all `x ∈ closure U`. -/
252: theorem norm_eqOn_closure_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn {f : E → F} {U : Set E} {c : E}
253:     (hc : IsPreconnected U) (ho : IsOpen U) (hd : DiffContOnCl ℂ f U) (hcU : c ∈ U)
254:     (hm : IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) U c) : EqOn (norm ∘ f) (const E ‖f c‖) (closure U) :=
255:   (norm_eqOn_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn hc ho hd.differentiableOn hcU hm).of_subset_closure
256:     hd.continuousOn.norm continuousOn_const subset_closure Subset.rfl
257: 
258: section StrictConvex
259: 
260: /-!
261: ### The case of a strictly convex codomain
262: 
263: If the codomain `F` is a strictly convex space, then we can claim equalities like `f w = f z`
264: instead of `‖f w‖ = ‖f z‖`.
265: 
266: Instead of repeating the proof starting with lemmas about integrals, we apply a corresponding lemma
267: above twice: for `f` and for `(f · + f c)`.  Then we have `‖f w‖ = ‖f z‖` and
268: `‖f w + f z‖ = ‖f z + f z‖`, thus `‖f w + f z‖ = ‖f w‖ + ‖f z‖`. This is only possible if
269: `f w = f z`, see `eq_of_norm_eq_of_norm_add_eq`.
270: -/
271: 
272: variable [StrictConvexSpace ℝ F]
273: 
274: /-- **Maximum modulus principle** on a connected set. Let `U` be a (pre)connected open set in a
275: complex normed space.  Let `f : E → F` be a function that is complex differentiable on `U`. Suppose
276: that `‖f x‖` takes its maximum value on `U` at `c ∈ U`. Then `f x = f c` for all `x ∈ U`.
277: 
278: TODO: change assumption from `IsMaxOn` to `IsLocalMax`. -/
279: theorem eqOn_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn_norm {f : E → F} {U : Set E} {c : E}
280:     (hc : IsPreconnected U) (ho : IsOpen U) (hd : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hcU : c ∈ U)
281:     (hm : IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) U c) : EqOn f (const E (f c)) U := fun x hx =>
282:   have H₁ : ‖f x‖ = ‖f c‖ := norm_eqOn_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn hc ho hd hcU hm hx
283:   have H₂ : ‖f x + f c‖ = ‖f c + f c‖ :=
284:     norm_eqOn_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn hc ho (hd.add_const _) hcU hm.norm_add_self hx
285:   eq_of_norm_eq_of_norm_add_eq H₁ <| by simp only [H₂, SameRay.rfl.norm_add, H₁, Function.const]
286: 
287: /-- **Maximum modulus principle** on a connected set. Let `U` be a (pre)connected open set in a
288: complex normed space.  Let `f : E → F` be a function that is complex differentiable on `U` and is
289: continuous on its closure. Suppose that `‖f x‖` takes its maximum value on `U` at `c ∈ U`. Then
290: `f x = f c` for all `x ∈ closure U`. -/
291: theorem eqOn_closure_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn_norm {f : E → F} {U : Set E} {c : E}
292:     (hc : IsPreconnected U) (ho : IsOpen U) (hd : DiffContOnCl ℂ f U) (hcU : c ∈ U)
293:     (hm : IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) U c) : EqOn f (const E (f c)) (closure U) :=
294:   (eqOn_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn_norm hc ho hd.differentiableOn hcU hm).of_subset_closure
295:     hd.continuousOn continuousOn_const subset_closure Subset.rfl
296: 
297: /-- **Maximum modulus principle**. Let `f : E → F` be a function between complex normed spaces.
298: Suppose that the codomain `F` is a strictly convex space, `f` is complex differentiable on a set
299: `s`, `f` is continuous on the closure of `s`, the norm of `f` takes it maximum on `s` at `z`, and
300: `w` is a point such that the closed ball with center `z` and radius `dist w z` is included in `s`,
301: then `f w = f z`. -/
302: theorem eq_of_isMaxOn_of_ball_subset {f : E → F} {s : Set E} {z w : E} (hd : DiffContOnCl ℂ f s)
303:     (hz : IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) s z) (hsub : ball z (dist w z) ⊆ s) : f w = f z :=
304:   have H₁ : ‖f w‖ = ‖f z‖ := norm_eq_norm_of_isMaxOn_of_ball_subset hd hz hsub
305:   have H₂ : ‖f w + f z‖ = ‖f z + f z‖ :=
306:     norm_eq_norm_of_isMaxOn_of_ball_subset (hd.add_const _) hz.norm_add_self hsub
307:   eq_of_norm_eq_of_norm_add_eq H₁ <| by simp only [H₂, SameRay.rfl.norm_add, H₁]
308: 
309: /-- **Maximum modulus principle** on a closed ball. Suppose that a function `f : E → F` from a
310: normed complex space to a strictly convex normed complex space has the following properties:
311: 
312: - it is continuous on a closed ball `Metric.closedBall z r`,
313: - it is complex differentiable on the corresponding open ball;
314: - the norm `‖f w‖` takes its maximum value on the open ball at its center.
315: 
316: Then `f` is a constant on the closed ball. -/
317: theorem eqOn_closedBall_of_isMaxOn_norm {f : E → F} {z : E} {r : ℝ}
318:     (hd : DiffContOnCl ℂ f (ball z r)) (hz : IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) (ball z r) z) :
319:     EqOn f (const E (f z)) (closedBall z r) := fun _x hx =>
320:   eq_of_isMaxOn_of_ball_subset hd hz <| ball_subset_ball hx
321: 
322: /-- If `f` is differentiable on the open unit ball `{z : ℂ | ‖z‖ < 1}`, and `‖f‖` attains a maximum
323: in this open ball, then `f` is constant. -/
324: lemma eq_const_of_exists_max {f : E → F} {b : ℝ} (h_an : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 b))
325:     {v : E} (hv : v ∈ ball 0 b) (hv_max : IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) (ball 0 b) v) :
326:     Set.EqOn f (Function.const E (f v)) (ball 0 b) :=
327:   Complex.eqOn_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn_norm (convex_ball 0 b).isPreconnected
328:     isOpen_ball h_an hv hv_max
329: 
330: /-- If `f` is a function differentiable on the open unit ball, and there exists an `r < 1` such that
331: any value of `‖f‖` on the open ball is bounded above by some value on the closed ball of radius `r`,
332: then `f` is constant. -/
333: lemma eq_const_of_exists_le [ProperSpace E] {f : E → F} {r b : ℝ}
334:     (h_an : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 b)) (hr_nn : 0 ≤ r) (hr_lt : r < b)
335:     (hr : ∀ z, z ∈ (ball 0 b) → ∃ w, w ∈ closedBall 0 r ∧ ‖f z‖ ≤ ‖f w‖) :
336:     Set.EqOn f (Function.const E (f 0)) (ball 0 b) := by
337:   obtain ⟨x, hx_mem, hx_max⟩ := isCompact_closedBall (0 : E) r |>.exists_isMaxOn
338:     (nonempty_closedBall.mpr hr_nn)
339:     (h_an.continuousOn.mono <| closedBall_subset_ball hr_lt).norm
340:   suffices Set.EqOn f (Function.const E (f x)) (ball 0 b) by
341:     rwa [this (mem_ball_self (hr_nn.trans_lt hr_lt))]
342:   apply eq_const_of_exists_max h_an (closedBall_subset_ball hr_lt hx_mem) (fun z hz ↦ ?_)
343:   obtain ⟨w, hw, hw'⟩ := hr z hz
344:   exact hw'.trans (hx_max hw)
345: 
346: /-- **Maximum modulus principle**: if `f : E → F` is complex differentiable in a neighborhood of `c`
347: and the norm `‖f z‖` has a local maximum at `c`, then `f` is locally constant in a neighborhood
348: of `c`. -/
349: theorem eventually_eq_of_isLocalMax_norm {f : E → F} {c : E}
350:     (hd : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 c, DifferentiableAt ℂ f z) (hc : IsLocalMax (norm ∘ f) c) :
351:     ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝 c, f y = f c := by
352:   rcases nhds_basis_closedBall.eventually_iff.1 (hd.and hc) with ⟨r, hr₀, hr⟩
353:   exact nhds_basis_closedBall.eventually_iff.2
354:     ⟨r, hr₀, eqOn_closedBall_of_isMaxOn_norm (DifferentiableOn.diffContOnCl fun x hx =>
355:         (hr <| closure_ball_subset_closedBall hx).1.differentiableWithinAt) fun x hx =>
356:       (hr <| ball_subset_closedBall hx).2⟩
357: 
358: theorem eventually_eq_or_eq_zero_of_isLocalMin_norm {f : E → ℂ} {c : E}
359:     (hf : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 c, DifferentiableAt ℂ f z) (hc : IsLocalMin (norm ∘ f) c) :
360:     (∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 c, f z = f c) ∨ f c = 0 := by
361:   refine or_iff_not_imp_right.mpr fun h => ?_
362:   have h1 : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 c, f z ≠ 0 := hf.self_of_nhds.continuousAt.eventually_ne h
363:   have h2 : IsLocalMax (norm ∘ f)⁻¹ c := hc.inv (h1.mono fun z => norm_pos_iff.mpr)
364:   have h3 : IsLocalMax (norm ∘ f⁻¹) c := by refine h2.congr (Eventually.of_forall ?_); simp
365:   have h4 : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 c, DifferentiableAt ℂ f⁻¹ z := by filter_upwards [hf, h1] with z h using h.inv
366:   filter_upwards [eventually_eq_of_isLocalMax_norm h4 h3] with z using inv_inj.mp

368: end StrictConvex
369: 
370: /-!
371: ### Maximum on a set vs maximum on its frontier
372: 
373: In this section we prove corollaries of the maximum modulus principle that relate the values of a
374: function on a set to its values on the frontier of this set.
375: -/
376: 
377: 
378: variable [Nontrivial E]
379: 
380: /-- **Maximum modulus principle**: if `f : E → F` is complex differentiable on a nonempty bounded
381: set `U` and is continuous on its closure, then there exists a point `z ∈ frontier U` such that
382: `(‖f ·‖)` takes it maximum value on `closure U` at `z`. -/
383: theorem exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_norm [FiniteDimensional ℂ E] {f : E → F} {U : Set E}
384:     (hb : IsBounded U) (hne : U.Nonempty) (hd : DiffContOnCl ℂ f U) :
385:     ∃ z ∈ frontier U, IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) (closure U) z := by
386:   have hc : IsCompact (closure U) := hb.isCompact_closure
387:   obtain ⟨w, hwU, hle⟩ : ∃ w ∈ closure U, IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) (closure U) w :=
388:     hc.exists_isMaxOn hne.closure hd.continuousOn.norm
389:   rw [closure_eq_interior_union_frontier, mem_union] at hwU
390:   rcases hwU with hwU | hwU; rotate_left; · exact ⟨w, hwU, hle⟩
391:   have : interior U ≠ univ := ne_top_of_le_ne_top hc.ne_univ interior_subset_closure
392:   rcases exists_mem_frontier_infDist_compl_eq_dist hwU this with ⟨z, hzU, hzw⟩
393:   refine ⟨z, frontier_interior_subset hzU, fun x hx => (hle hx).out.trans_eq ?_⟩
394:   refine (norm_eq_norm_of_isMaxOn_of_ball_subset hd (hle.on_subset subset_closure) ?_).symm
395:   rw [dist_comm, ← hzw]
396:   exact ball_infDist_compl_subset.trans interior_subset
397: 
398: /-- **Maximum modulus principle**: if `f : E → F` is complex differentiable on a bounded set `U` and
399: `‖f z‖ ≤ C` for any `z ∈ frontier U`, then the same is true for any `z ∈ closure U`. -/
400: theorem norm_le_of_forall_mem_frontier_norm_le {f : E → F} {U : Set E} (hU : IsBounded U)
401:     (hd : DiffContOnCl ℂ f U) {C : ℝ} (hC : ∀ z ∈ frontier U, ‖f z‖ ≤ C) {z : E}
402:     (hz : z ∈ closure U) : ‖f z‖ ≤ C := by
403:   rw [closure_eq_self_union_frontier, union_comm, mem_union] at hz
404:   rcases hz with hz | hz; · exact hC z hz
405:   /- In case of a finite-dimensional domain, one can just apply
406:     `Complex.exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_norm`. To make it work in any Banach space, we restrict
407:     the function to a line first. -/
408:   rcases exists_ne z with ⟨w, hne⟩
409:   set e := (lineMap z w : ℂ → E)
410:   have hde : Differentiable ℂ e := (differentiable_id.smul_const (w - z)).add_const z
411:   have hL : AntilipschitzWith (nndist z w)⁻¹ e := antilipschitzWith_lineMap hne.symm
412:   replace hd : DiffContOnCl ℂ (f ∘ e) (e ⁻¹' U) :=
413:     hd.comp hde.diffContOnCl (mapsTo_preimage _ _)
414:   have h₀ : (0 : ℂ) ∈ e ⁻¹' U := by simpa only [e, mem_preimage, lineMap_apply_zero]
415:   rcases exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_norm (hL.isBounded_preimage hU) ⟨0, h₀⟩ hd with ⟨ζ, hζU, hζ⟩
416:   calc
417:     ‖f z‖ = ‖f (e 0)‖ := by simp only [e, lineMap_apply_zero]
418:     _ ≤ ‖f (e ζ)‖ := hζ (subset_closure h₀)
419:     _ ≤ C := hC _ (hde.continuous.frontier_preimage_subset _ hζU)
420: 
421: /-- If two complex differentiable functions `f g : E → F` are equal on the boundary of a bounded set
422: `U`, then they are equal on `closure U`. -/
423: theorem eqOn_closure_of_eqOn_frontier {f g : E → F} {U : Set E} (hU : IsBounded U)
424:     (hf : DiffContOnCl ℂ f U) (hg : DiffContOnCl ℂ g U) (hfg : EqOn f g (frontier U)) :
425:     EqOn f g (closure U) := by
426:   suffices H : ∀ z ∈ closure U, ‖(f - g) z‖ ≤ 0 by simpa [sub_eq_zero] using H
427:   refine fun z hz => norm_le_of_forall_mem_frontier_norm_le hU (hf.sub hg) (fun w hw => ?_) hz
428:   simp [hfg hw]
429: 
430: /-- If two complex differentiable functions `f g : E → F` are equal on the boundary of a bounded set
431: `U`, then they are equal on `U`. -/
432: theorem eqOn_of_eqOn_frontier {f g : E → F} {U : Set E} (hU : IsBounded U) (hf : DiffContOnCl ℂ f U)
433:     (hg : DiffContOnCl ℂ g U) (hfg : EqOn f g (frontier U)) : EqOn f g U :=
434:   (eqOn_closure_of_eqOn_frontier hU hf hg hfg).mono subset_closure
435:
